intro: Bootstrap resampling repeatedly draws observations with replacement. Supplied draws separate the statistic from random-number generation.
task: Compute one mean per supplied bootstrap resample and the sample standard deviation of those means.
requirements: values is a length-n vector. indices is an integer-valued (b,n) matrix with b>=2 and entries in [0,n-1]. Repeated indices are valid.
Return {"means": mean(values[indices],axis=1), "standard_error": standard deviation of those means with ddof=1}.
Do not generate randomness, deduplicate indices, or divide the standard deviation by sqrt(b). The resample distribution estimates estimator variability.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Two resamples
Repeated index draws
Same means

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Indexing with the supplied matrix creates one complete resample per row, including repeated positions.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: The spread of those row means is the estimate; use the sample standard deviation without another square-root scaling.

explanation: A bootstrap row samples original observation positions with replacement. Repeated positions remain repeated because multiplicity is part of the resampling distribution.
The spread across resample means estimates uncertainty in the mean estimator. Dividing it by the square root of the number of resamples instead describes Monte Carlo precision.
